summary.headline: Gallantt FY26 consolidated revenue INR 4,418.92 crore (+3.95% YoY) with EBITDA per ton up to INR 8,785 from INR 8,300; net debt-free.
summary.overview: FY26 was described by management as a consolidation year with volume growth of 1.7%, while EBITDA margin reached 17.56% and PAT margin 10.81%. Q4 FY26 revenue was INR 1,204.81 crore, up 12.93% QoQ, with EBITDA margin of 16.99% versus 15.5% in Q3. The company reported net cash of about INR 360 crore after INR 440 crore of borrowings, mostly working-capital lines. Management outlined a INR 3,000 crore capex plan (steel capacity 1.0 to 1.3 million tonnes, mines, solar) funded from internal accruals, with a medium-term growth plan to be presented in Q2 FY27.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 168.69 crore and 15.5% in Q3
Borrowings INR 440 crore; surplus about INR 800 crore as of 31 Mar 2026

segments.name: Steel (integrated: pellets, sponge iron, billet, TMT)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 production: pellets 222 kt, sponge iron 245 kt, billet 235 kt, TMT 210 kt. FY26 production: pellets 819 kt, sponge iron 915 kt, billet 883 kt, TMT 788 kt.

segments.name: Sales volumes (FY26)
segments.commentary: Pellets sold 49 kt, sponge iron sold 125 kt, billet sold 81 kt, TMT bar sold 766 kt. Most upstream output is consumed internally; management aims to lower the share sold externally.

guidance_outlook: Capex plan of INR 3,000 crore: steel capacity expansion from 1.0 to 1.3 million tonnes at about INR 1,200 crore, due H2 FY27 (management said completion in current FY).
Solar capex about INR 225-300 crore: 18 MW at Gujarat (Sidhpur) by Q2 FY27, 60 MW at Gorakhpur/Prayagraj by Q4 FY27; expected annual savings INR 30-40 crore.
Captive mines in Rajasthan and UP (four mines allotted) with about INR 1,500 crore capex, targeted by FY28; expected EBITDA gain about INR 2,000 per ton.
Revenue expected to rise to roughly INR 5,300-5,400 crore after expansion; EBITDA margin guided to around 20% with mining integration (currently 15-17%).
Medium-term growth plan to be presented in Q2 FY27.
Leverage expected to remain comfortable through FY27; capex to be funded from internal accruals, with no equity in the INR 3,000 crore programme per management.
capex_capacity: Steel capacity expansion 1.0 to 1.3 million tonnes, about INR 1,200 crore, underway, production expected H2 FY27.
Solar: 18 MW Gujarat (Sidhpur) and 60 MW Gorakhpur (Prayagraj area), total 78 MW, self-consumed; about INR 225-300 crore.
Mines: four allotted in UP and Rajasthan, about INR 1,500 crore, completion targeted FY28, subject to approvals.
Capacity utilisation about 88% currently (previously about 80%); management expects 90-92% as a good level.
Gujarat upstream de-bottlenecking capex in current FY expected to lift EBITDA per ton.
demand_pricing: Raw material cost held at about 72% of net realisation in both FY25 and FY26 despite coal and iron ore volatility.
Company claims about 25% market share in its UP and Gujarat selling areas and a brand-driven premium over peers.
Iron ore sourcing: Gorakhpur uses fines from Odisha, MP and some Maharashtra; Gujarat uses pellets from Rajasthan, NMDC long-term offtake, and imports when viable.
Management sees no near-term case for exports unless export realisations are clearly better than domestic; no geographic expansion beyond UP and Gujarat in the short-to-medium term.
Management described softer realisations during FY26 with EBITDA/ton still improving.

qa_highlights.question: Where do you see the company in 2-3 years, in terms of top-line and bottom-line growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Post the INR 3,000 crore expansion to 1.3 million tonnes, revenue should rise to about INR 5,300-5,400 crore with lower costs; a second phase medium- to long-term plan to be announced around Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What margins do you expect?
qa_highlights.answer: Currently 15-17%; with project completion and mining integration, management expects around 20%.

qa_highlights.question: How is capex funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Largely internal accruals; management later clarified there is no equity component in the INR 3,000 crore programme, though it said it would consider debt and equity where appropriate.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY26 volume figures and capex timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: Production and sales volumes were given by product (see segments). Steel capacity expansion in H2 FY27, solar by FY27 end, mines by FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is done with the cash surplus of about INR 800 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Surplus is treated as temporary; about INR 360 crore net cash, part deployed in intercorporate deposits at 12% payable on demand within three months; cash to go mainly to capex and partly dividends.

qa_highlights.question: What is the peak utilisation and optimum capacity level?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation has risen to 88% from about 80% earlier; management targets 90-92%.

risks_watch: Intercorporate deposits of about INR 360 crore at 12% payable on demand within three months; counterparty exposure was asserted as low but is a disclosure point to monitor.
Execution risk on INR 1,500 crore mine development targeted for FY28, pending approvals; management acknowledged Indian mining approvals are slow.

Implementation of the INR 3,000 crore programme and the later medium-term plan; management flagged balanced funding (equity and external borrowing) as a possible requirement, which conflicts with the 'internal accruals only' statement.
Raw material and iron ore cost volatility, currency impact on imports, and dependence on coal and iron ore pricing.
Reliance on UP and Gujarat markets; no near-term geographic diversification.

Q4 volume figures shared on the call (pellet, sponge iron, billet, TMT) were not in the prepared remarks; sales volume gap between production and sales for pellets and sponge iron (FY26 pellet produced 819 kt vs sold 49 kt) needs clarification.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on long-term demand and margin targets (about 20% EBITDA margin, INR 2,000/ton mining saving), but more hedged on timelines, with several answers saying approvals and implementation are still pending. Mild inconsistency on funding: 'internal accruals only' versus openness to debt and equity.
key_quotes: We are evaluating a medium-term growth plan alongside the ongoing INR 3,000 crores capex program and intend to present this opportunity in Q2 FY27.
Every rupee of capital expenditure incurred over the past five years, which is about INR 1,200 crores approximately in total, has been funded entirely through internal accruals.
Gallantt is a net cash surplus generating company. We carry no term loans and our borrowings are limited to working capital facilities deployed in the normal course of operations.

adds.what: Steel capacity expansion 1.0 to 1.3 million tonnes/yr (about 0.3 Mt) under INR 3,000 cr plan
Solar 78 MW (18 MW Sidhpur Gujarat + 60 MW Gorakhpur/Prayagraj), self-consumed
Four captive mines in Rajasthan and UP, subject to approvals

growth.why: Management guides revenue to INR 5,300-5,400 cr post-expansion (about 20-22% above FY26's INR 4,419 cr), backed by a 1.0 to 1.3 Mt steel capacity addition due H2 FY27 and mines targeted FY28, though the brief gives no timing-specific orders and the growth-plan detail is deferred to Q2 FY27.
